title: Continuous Performance Monitoring
description: Build a production performance monitoring strategy using Real User Monitoring, synthetic testing, performance budgets, and alerting.

data.text: Performance does not stay good by accident. It requires continuous measurement: field data from real users, synthetic tests in CI, and alerts when budgets are breached. Without monitoring, regressions ship silently and compound over time.

RUM collects performance data from actual visitors across devices, networks, and geographies. It reveals problems that lab tests miss, such as slow 3G experiences, low-end device jank, and regional CDN failures.

data.title: Production RUM Implementation
data.content: Send Core Web Vitals and custom timings to analytics.

data.text: Synthetic tests run on a schedule from fixed locations using controlled hardware and network profiles. They catch regressions before users do. Combine Lighthouse CI, WebPageTest, and custom Playwright scripts for comprehensive coverage.

data.title: Lighthouse CI Configuration
data.content: Run Lighthouse in CI with budgets and assertions.

data.text: A performance budget is a hard limit on a measurable quantity: bundle size, total JS, images, requests, or a Core Web Vital. Budgets stop regressions at the pull-request level. The best budgets are tied to user-facing metrics, not arbitrary byte counts.

data.title: Bundle and Metric Budgets
data.content: Define and enforce performance budgets in CI.

data.text: Dashboards show trends; alerts catch sudden regressions. Page oncall or a dedicated performance channel should receive alerts when field metrics cross a threshold. Alert on sustained degradation, not one-off outliers, to avoid noise.

data.title: Alerting Strategy
data.content: Design alerts that are actionable but not noisy.
data.code:
Recommended alerting rules:

Core Web Vitals degradation:
- Trigger: p75 LCP or INP increases >20% for 1 hour
- Severity: page-critical
- Channel: #web-performance
- Runbook: link to performance dashboard + last deploy

CLS regression:
- Trigger: p75 CLS > 0.1 for 30 minutes
- Severity: high
- Channel: #web-performance

Bundle size regression:
- Trigger: main bundle exceeds budget by >5%
- Severity: high
- Channel: PR comment + engineering channel

Third-party script regression:
- Trigger: script evaluation time increases >2x
- Severity: medium
- Channel: #web-performance

Dashboard views:
- Core Web Vitals by device type and geography
- Largest contributors to INP
- LCP element and URL breakdown
- Deploy marker overlay on metrics timelines

data.text: Gate deploys on performance budgets. Run Lighthouse in CI, compare bundle sizes, and fail the build when budgets are breached. Pair this with post-deploy smoke tests using Playwright to catch render-blocking issues.

data.title: CI Performance Gate
data.code:
# GitHub Actions example
- name: Lighthouse CI
  run: |
    npm install -g @lhci/cli@0.14
    lhci collect --url=http://localhost:3000
    lhci upload --target=temporary-public-storage
    lhci assert --assertions.budget=performance-budgets.config.js

- name: Bundle size check
  run: |
    npm run build
    npx size-limit

- name: Playwright smoke test
  run: npx playwright test tests/smoke-performance.spec.ts

data.title: Start Small, Then Scale
data.text: You do not need every tool on day one. Start with RUM for Core Web Vitals, add a Lighthouse budget in CI, then layer on synthetic tests and alerting. Iterate on coverage rather than trying to instrument everything at once.

terms.definition: Collecting performance data from real user sessions to measure field performance.
A hard limit on a performance metric enforced in CI to prevent regressions.
Automated tests that simulate user interactions and measure performance from controlled environments.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: RUM measures real user experience across devices, networks, and geographies
Synthetic tests catch regressions before users notice
Performance budgets stop regressions at the CI level
Use web-vitals for reliable Core Web Vitals field measurement
Use Lighthouse CI for automated audits and budget assertions
Alert on sustained degradation, not outliers
Start with Core Web Vitals RUM, then add synthetic and CI budgets
data.takeaway: Continuous monitoring turns performance into a measurable, maintainable property. Combine RUM, synthetic testing, budgets, and alerting to catch regressions early and keep the user experience predictable.
